hiddenBlocks.note: v5 R1, mystery blocks: the lookahead player scores each tap as the mean over this many boards with the hidden blocks' colours dealt again among them (tools/grade.js look), so it never sees where a hidden colour is.

note: Sapper's Path bake (SPEC-v3 §5; v4 M3, the Siege to 100; v4.1, castle pictures entered from the bottom; v4.2, full-screen boards from level 26, sized for a 375x812 phone at 8 CSS px a cell, and real-pace times). Bands are Normal random-tap win rates. maxTaps caps the taps in any level (a linked pair is one tap, two cards). maxWaitMs: the dead-time cap, the longest single tap on the stored Normal line (patient play, from a tap until nothing moves). lookahead: the one-move-lookahead player's Normal win-rate target for late hard slots (a pick over it is logged). colours: [from, to, min, max] per level range (a picture needs 4: sky, grass, the black outline and its walls). dealBy and genBy override deal/era params per band kind or slot. twists: which generated levels carry mystery cards, linked pairs and the lock (twistsOf in bake.js). fast: the fast tapper's check. mystery: the '?' flags and the sampling planner that measures them. eras[e].gen: the era's castle picture (tools/castle.js; w and h are the picture's columns and rows without its frame). picture: the pictures' frame, palette and roles (tools/castle.js, tools/pic.js). Holding spaces per tag live in config.json v3.rules. v4.3: every level has one fixed tag (tags) and is graded, banded and timed on it alone; the bands follow the tag (curve.byTag).

relay.note: v5 R2, the re-lay (tools/relay.js; bake.js --relay): src, the commit whose level files are the v4.3 source; drop, the old levels left out (Era 1's spare, 25: a 20 x 22 board can't reach the 3-minute target that holds from level 26); teach, the new teaching slots and the old teaching level each reuses (25 moats <- the locked-bridge lesson, its drawbridge opened; 50 gates and keys <- the linked lesson, towers plain and links dropped; 75 linked squads <- All at Once, towers plain, flags and lock dropped; 100 mystery cards <- the Hidden Colours lesson as it is); teachEdits, their edits; lockAt, where a Hard level's colour lock sits (the colour whose first squad comes nearest this fraction of the order); cost, the slot map's weights (tag: a slot whose tag differs from the board's v4.3 tag; small: a reused teaching board off an Easy slot; edit: each edit; move: per level moved; links: a Hard Twinspire slot whose board has no links; keyLock: a key lock that stays, a bonus; infeasible: a slot the board can't fill; newBoard: the new board's cost anywhere).

tags.note: v4.3 (tools/tags.js): every level plays on one fixed tag; no difficulty picker. Teaching levels: first before from, afterEnd at a realm's first level (its milestone lesson), else teach (never Hard). Other levels before from: first; then cycle repeating. v5 R2: realms (the rules review's feature ladder: The Greenmarch 1-24, Fenwater Vale 25-49, The Ironhollows 50-74, Twinspire Reach 75-99, The Mistmoor from 100): every realm ends on a Hard level, its first level teaches its new feature (Easy), and the cycle restarts after it (realm 1 keeps from, so 1-24 carry v4.3's tags). The tag no longer changes any rule (5 spaces on every level); it says how many features a level uses (config.json v5.density). ends: the realm ends, kept for the report. Siege 1-100: 15 easy, 62 normal, 23 hard.
tags.v6Note: Campaign v6 stage 2 (the approved curve, tools/campaign-v6-curve.md; tools/tags.js tagOf): v6 is the tag of levels 1-200, one letter a level (E easy, N normal, H hard, X extreme), laid out per realm by the curve's counts and its sawtooth (a Normal lead, a Hard run to an Extreme peak, an Easy breather after a peak; each realm ends on Extreme) within what each board can carry (a key board is Hard or Extreme; Easy needs a board with at most one feature; Extreme from 50 a gate, from 125 towers); 53 stays the first colour lock and 87 the first key lock (their coach lines). Past 200 the schedule below.
tags.cyclesNote: v5 R4 (tools/tags.js): realms 6-8 run their own cycle (keyed by the realm's first level; start: the first level the cycle covers, after a lesson) and end on endTag; the rules review: 125-149 Hard-led with Extreme appearing, 150-200 Hard and Extreme, a couple of Easy breathers a realm, 200 the boss (Extreme). Realm 5 (101-124): about a third Hard (the ladder), ending Hard.

eras.note: v5 R2: an era is a realm of the journey (bake-config tags.realms; config.json eras names them); each realm's castle look is the matching v4 era's generator (realm 1 stockades, 2 moated mottes, 3 stone keeps, 4 concentric castles).

5.note: v5 R2: The Mistmoor (100-124); level 100 reuses a teaching board. v5 R4: stilt forts over the fen (tools/castle.js era5). The plan sets moat, gates and towers per level (bake-config plan).

6.note: v5 R4: Emberwatch Crags, basalt forts on volcanic heights (tools/castle.js era6); the moat is a lava channel (liquid lava).

7.note: v5 R4: The Shrouded Weald, living-wood strongholds in an enchanted forest by moonlight (tools/castle.js era7).

8.note: v5 R4: The Goblin King's Throne, the goblin capital: a crooked fortress of mismatched stone and scrap (tools/castle.js era8); 200 is the boss (bosses).

boss.note: v5 R2: the old boss board ends Twinspire Reach at 99 (the Goblin King's throne is 200, R4). Level 99, the boss: a full-screen concentric castle at night, both moats with their drawbridges, four towers on the outer curtain and three or four on the inner, every twist, twelve colours.

plan.note: v5 R4 (bake.js planOf; the rules review: tags mean how many of the unlocked features a level uses, config.json v5.density): from level `from` every generated level's features are planned from its tag. Extreme: every unlocked feature and the lock. Hard: every one before hardFrom; from hardFrom all but one with probability hardDrop (a seeded drop among linked, mystery, tower, hidden, gate), and the lock. Normal: normal[0] features, one more with probability normalMore (never all). Easy: none with probability easyNone, else one (never a gate: a gate is a drawbridge and needs its moat). A gate brings its moat; with probability twoGates a Hard or Extreme level has a second gate. The lock is a key lock with probability keyLock, else a colour lock (the colour whose first squad comes nearest relay.lockAt of the dealt order; the dealer plays it shut). towers: archer towers per tag; hidden: mystery blocks (gen.js hide: share of the castle's eligible blocks, blob radii, the least accepted); colours: the castle's colour range per realm (it counts the gilt keys and the towers' slate when the plan has them). Every draw is hash01(n, k), fixed by the level number.

hidden.fixNote: v5 R4 fix (the visual critic S3, levels 175-200 re-baked): hidden blocks only on the fortress walls (never the sky, clouds or the black outline, so the silhouette reads; never the gold, banners or red roofs, so the crown, the flags and the boss's king stay in sight), smaller blobs, a lower share and no 4-connected group of more than maxGroup cells. Levels 150-174 keep the R4 bake (share 0.18-0.32, blobs 3-6 x 2-4, no skip or cap).

r4fix.note: v5 R4 (bake.js --r4fix): the fix-up run's lighter search for the Extreme and hardest levels of 125-200 the full run lost to two bugs (an Extreme tag with no rules in the bake; a colour lock's stand-in compiled before its deck). The tuner's narrowing stage (the one-move-lookahead hill-climb) dominates on these boards (towers, locks, links: about 3 minutes a candidate, 30 candidates a level), so the fix-up tries fewer candidates and a shorter, lighter climb. Every target is still graded in full (the lookahead's 25% included); only the search is smaller.

bosses.note: v5 R4: per-level bosses (bake.js bossOf; boss stays the old one at 99). 200, the Goblin King's throne: the biggest board (40 x 41 picture, two rows taller than the realm's), both moats with their drawbridges (inner), 3-4 archer towers, every feature, eleven or twelve colours. (A 42 x 43 board with 4-5 towers would not deal inside the 55-tap and 15 s caps: 0 of 8 forts in a trial, tools/v5-r4-notes.md.)

late.note: pattern names the slots before tags (v4.2); from v4.3 the tag picks the slot (byTag) and only the boss override stands.

byTag.note: v4.3: the band follows the tag. mid: easy takes saw slot 0, hard slot 2, normal keeps its saw slot but never past cap (1). late: easy takes relief, normal hard, hard hardest (the boss stays boss). Levels 1-15 are early on every tag.

duration.note: Patient play-through time at 1x (engine ms) on the stored Normal winning line: tap, wait until every squad is home, tap again. Picks prefer candidates inside the limits; a pick outside is logged as a fallback. The median target is met by the generator sizes and squad sizes (v3.time only sets the swarm).

pace.note: v4.2, the real-pace measure (grade.pace): the stored Normal winning order replayed, each next card tapped the moment a space is free, then times factor (Peter's pace, calibrated on the v4.1 levels: tools/v4.2-notes.md). From level `from`, picks prefer candidates whose real pace is inside range (the boss: boss); a replay that loses falls back to the patient time and is logged. The patient maxMs now applies to levels before `from` only (patient times are still reported). v4.3: the replay runs on the level's own tag; a lost replay counts as a duration miss. aim: among candidates meeting every target the picker prefers the real pace nearest aim (aimWeight ms from it weigh as one point of rate from the band's middle). thinks: the replay is also run waiting this many ms after each tap (reported; on a tie the picker prefers more of them won).
pace.steadyNote: Land 1 fix (the functional critic's m2, m3): steady, the think time (ms) of the steady-rhythm replay graded on every land level (grade.steady: its longest wait between two taps and from the last tap to the end; tools/land-bake.js gates the wait between taps at maxWaitMs and every thinking replay won).

fast.note: The fast tapper (grade.fast: taps a random legal card the moment one exists). From level `from` on, a level is much easier tapped fast when fast - patient >= pts, or fast > ratio x patient and fast - patient >= minPts; the picker prefers candidates that pass.

twists.note: Generated levels from `from` carry the twist with probability p (fixed per level), forced after `gap` levels without it; from mixFrom every level carries at least one. mystery.cards: '?' flags per level; links.pairs: linked pairs per level. v5 R2: the froms follow the feature ladder (linked 75, mystery cards 100, the lock 50 on Hard levels only); the re-lay (bake.js --relay) sets each level's twists from its slot and tag instead (tools/relay.js), so this schedule only drives a plain bake.

mystery.note: '?' flags go on cards dealt in rows rows[0]-rows[1] of their column (0 = the front), never a linked card, never two in a row in one column. Each placement is measured by the sampling planner (grade.plan: games games, samples colourings per decision), honest and all-seeing; the first within maxGap is kept, else the smallest gap after tries (one flag fewer each try, never under 2).

coloursNote: v5 R2: the ranges follow the realms (v4.3 left the teaching levels 26 and 51 out; 26 and 51 are generated slots now).

dealByLevel.note: v4.3: a level's own deal overrides, applied after the slot's (fix-up runs: --only N-N --keep FILE, merged with --merge). 53: its board needs the biggest of 3 colours per squad to deal inside the 55-tap cap (1 in 24 attempts deals even then). 83: an Easy breather on an Era 4 board whose deals run short on 6 spaces; the biggest of 3 and more squads dealt before they can reach bring its real pace from 160 s to 168 s (still under 180 s: the one reported fallback, tools/v4.3-notes.md).

careful.note: Land 1 fix (the functional critic's M1): the careful player (tools/grade.js careful: thinks depth taps ahead at rest, sees every hidden card and block), games per level, graded on every land main level (tools/land-bake.js gradeLevel; tools/regrade.js checks it where a level stores it). The castle's levels never stored it.
careful.v6Note: Campaign v6 stage 1: byRange sets the games per level range (tools/grade.js carefulGames: the last entry holding the level wins; 32 from 150 to 200); castle turns the careful player on in bake.js gradeLevel for the castle levels (off until stage 2; regrade.js checks it wherever a level stores it).

obvious.note: Land 1 fix (the functional critic's m1): the obvious player, the careful player one tap deep (send the squad that leaves the fewest blocks at rest, skip a tap that jams), games per level; graded on every land main level (grade.obvious), gated per tag by the land's profile.

genBy.note: Per slot: scale the era's picture sides (per era). Early levels (4-15) and Era 1's reliefs are smaller, and quicker; from level 26 every board fills the phone (v4.2).

penalty.note: Fallback picks (no candidate meets every target): the least total of band miss x band (per unit rate), duration miss / durationMs, dead-time miss / waitMs, fast x a fast-tapper flag, pairs x a missing pair, lookahead over its target / lookahead.

dealNote: v5 R2, the dealer for 5 spaces with archers that only knock back: deal.hold 5, the same spaces every level plays on (v4.3 dealt on Hard's 4 so a deal won on every tag); a lock deals with one open space fewer until it opens (key: its pixel pops; colour: the dealer leaves it shut, so a deal never leans on it). rushHard false: rushed dealing existed because a Hard kill left a colour short; with no kills a player tapping the moment a space frees can never run short, so it goes. Dealing mode still fails a deal at any arrow hit (reason hit), so deals stay hit-free, and noParkUnderArchers stays (a squad parked under a ring would be hit when released). deal.park: at most this many squads wait on the line at rest; v4.1 deal.parkMax: none of them with more than this many sappers (a big squad parked behind a gate pours out when the gate opens, and far from the entry square every round of it is a long walk, so the tap that opened the gate would run past the dead-time cap). v4.2: dealBy mid and late deal squads of 90-99 (they shrink by deal.shrink, deal.shrinks times, where a tap would pass the dead-time cap); best: each squad is the biggest of the first `best` colours that fit (1, the default, deals as before); attempts: deal attempts a candidate. v4.3 deal.rushHard: a Hard level whose archers stand is dealt rushed (gen.js D.rush): a second simulation taps each squad the moment a space is free beside the patient one, so its stored order also wins at real pace (a Hard kill is a short fail). v4.3 dealBy.era<e> (applied after the kind, before the slot): a space now frees at its squad's last pickup, so levels run about a quarter quicker on the same board; from Era 2 the deal takes the first colour that fits (best 1, not the biggest of 3) and lets up to 3 squads wait at rest (park 3; Era 2 also deals a squad that cannot reach yet first 30% of the time), which keeps more squads waiting on the line and brings the real pace back toward its v4.2 target (tools/v4.3-notes.md).

picture.note: v4.1 castle pictures (tools/castle.js, tools/pic.js). entryHalf: the entry square is the bottom frame row's cells within this many of its middle (3 cells on an odd width, 2 on an even one). minDE, fadeDE: every pair of a picture's colours (gilt keys and the black outline included) should be this far apart in CIEDE2000, plain and with one faded to a queue row behind the front (config.json layout.fade); the role colours were searched for it and every pair of roles that can stand together meets both. starts: the palette search's starts (pic.js choose). ink: the outline black; iron: the drawbridge and portcullis (gates); show: the colours tools/castle.js --sheet draws open ground, the entry, water and gates in. roles: each role's name (a crew's name where the page reads one) and its colour. eras[e]: the roles every picture of the era has (must), the optional ones added in a seeded order until the level's colour count is reached (opt; `first` ahead of the rest), and the colour count tools/castle.js --sheet samples. v4.1 fix: scenes (the visual critic's V1, lever 4): pre-checked scene palettes (tools/palette.js --scenes), each for the eras listed, its colours (c) and crew names (n) over the roles' for the roles it changes, the roles it drops (drop: clouds at dawn on stone castles and in winter), moon (a moon and stars in the cloud role instead of the sun) and pine (pine trees); eras[e].scenes weights the era's scenes (the boss's gen names its own).

variety.note: v4.1 fix (the visual critic's V1 gate; tools/variety.js): how alike two castle pictures of one era are is the share of a cols x rows grid of picture cells (the frame left out) whose colours match. The bake picks a candidate meeting every target only if its median match against its era's earlier generated picks is maxMedian or under (else the least alike of them, logged), and reports every era's median over all its pairs; tools/test.js checks every era's median is maxMedian or under.

v6.note: Campaign v6 stage 2, the re-deal of 1-200 (tools/campaign-v6.js, tools/campaign-v6-bake.js; the approved curve tools/campaign-v6-curve.md). bands: the random-tap band per tag. care: the careful player's ceiling per tag by level range (ranges: [from, to] each; null: none; boss: level 200's); levels before tutorial[1] keep their decks (a gentle tutorial, no band or ceiling). pace: real pace range per level (realm 1: short boards; boss: 200's), the aim the pick leans to, and median, the curve's gate on each realm's median from realm 2 (a locked, pinned or killing level runs longer, so a level may run past 300 s where its realm stays inside). candidates: per level by tag (--extra K adds K); the kept deck is candidate -1 when the board and locks are unchanged. deal: the dealer's params over bake-config deal (base, then byRealm, then byTag; deepAlt/sizeAlt: candidate k takes entry k mod length). tune.careful: gen.js carefulStage (games by byRange, toward under x the ceiling). hidden: gen.js hide over plan.hidden (share from the plan, gap keeps blobs apart). lockAt: lock k's colour, the colour whose first squad comes nearest lockAt[k] of the order. careWeight: among good picks the careful rate weighs this many points of rate per 1.0; keptBonus: points a kept deck is preferred by. penalty: the fallback's weights. counts: each realm's E/N/H/X. towers, amounts (linked pairs, ? cards and mystery blocks by tag, each drawn by the level number), twoLocksFrom (Extreme carries two locks from here), coach (config.json teach entries whose card is the level's lock or tower colour, set on install), baseCommit (the levels before the re-deal, for the measure), mystery (? cards over bake-config mystery: rows behind the front, so 6-8 fit). dealByLevel: a level's own deal overrides (more attempts where deals are rare). swaps: tag swaps inside a realm (counts unchanged) where a level could not reach its ceiling, logged.

towers.note: restore: realms 3-4, the v4.3 board's towers (git relay.src; v5 R2 turned them plain); add: a slate tower painted at the frame on the bank path (campaign-v6.js paintTower: side, rows tall, range r); drop: towers turned plain; from dropFrom a Normal or Easy level drops its towers unless keep lists it. 64 is the first tower (Hard, pinning: its coach line), 66 the first kill. keepOnly: a killing level whose full set of towers leaves no deal whose order survives real pace keeps these (by index; measured over 30 deals a subset, tools/campaign-v6-notes.md §3).

swaps.why: 189's open board (no moat or gate) kept the careful player at 0.69 or more over 28 Hard candidates (ceiling 0.15); 188's moat, gate and tower carry the Hard (pin + lock), 189 plays Normal
